title: Python Foundations
description: A structured introduction to Python programming, covering syntax, data structures, and essential programming paradigms. Designed for learners with no prior programming experience who want to build a solid foundation before advancing to specialised domains.

steps.title: Environment Setup and Python Basics
steps.description: Install Python and configure a virtual environment with venv. Explore the REPL, write your first script, and understand how variables, built-in types (int, float, str, bool, NoneType), and operators work. Practice type introspection with type() and isinstance().

steps.title: Control Flow and Functions
steps.description: Master conditional logic (if/elif/else), loops (for, while, break, continue), and define reusable functions with positional, keyword, default, and *args/**kwargs parameters. Understand scope (LEGB rule) and first-class function concepts.

steps.title: Collections, Comprehensions, and File I/O
steps.description: Deep-dive into lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets. Write list and dictionary comprehensions for concise data transformation. Read and write text and CSV files using open() and the csv module. Handle common I/O exceptions gracefully.

steps.title: Modules, Packages, and Testing
steps.description: Organise code into modules and packages with __init__.py. Install third-party libraries with pip and understand dependency pinning via requirements.txt. Write unit tests with pytest, use assertions, and run coverage reports.

steps.title: Object-Oriented Programming in Python
steps.description: Understand the difference between classes and objects and how Python instantiates them via __init__. Define instance attributes, instance methods, class attributes, and class methods. Apply encapsulation by controlling access with name mangling and properties (getter/setter). Explore inheritance — single and multiple — and contrast it with composition as an alternative for code reuse. Use dataclasses as a concise syntax for data-centric classes.

title: Artificial Intelligence — From Concepts to Practice
description: A practical journey through the core pillars of modern AI: supervised learning, neural networks, natural language processing, and responsible deployment. Requires comfort with Python and basic linear algebra. Learners emerge able to build, evaluate, and explain end-to-end ML pipelines.

steps.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
steps.description: Understand the ML workflow: data collection, exploratory data analysis (EDA), preprocessing, model selection, training, and evaluation. Implement linear regression and k-nearest neighbours from scratch, then replicate with scikit-learn. Master train/validation/test splits and cross-validation strategies.

steps.title: Scikit-learn Pipelines and Classical Algorithms
steps.description: Build reproducible scikit-learn Pipelines that chain imputation, scaling, encoding, and classifier steps. Compare decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM), and SVMs. Use GridSearchCV and Optuna for hyperparameter tuning. Interpret models with SHAP values.

steps.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning with PyTorch
steps.description: Build feedforward networks with torch.nn. Understand backpropagation, optimisers (SGD, Adam), and regularisation (dropout, batch normalisation). Train a convolutional network on an image dataset and interpret loss/accuracy curves. Save and load checkpoints.

steps.title: Natural Language Processing and Transformers
steps.description: Tokenise text, compute TF-IDF embeddings, and fine-tune a pre-trained BERT model for text classification using the HuggingFace Transformers library. Evaluate with precision, recall, and F1. Explore zero-shot and few-shot inference with open models.

steps.title: Model Deployment and Responsible AI
steps.description: Expose a trained model as a REST API with FastAPI and Pydantic. Containerise with Docker and document the endpoint with OpenAPI. Conduct a bias audit using Fairlearn, document model cards, and discuss GDPR implications for ML systems.

title: AI Agent Development
description: A hands-on path covering the architecture and implementation of autonomous AI agents. Learners progress from prompt engineering fundamentals through tool-augmented agents, multi-agent systems, and production observability. Prior experience with Python and a working knowledge of LLMs is assumed.

steps.title: Prompt Engineering and LLM APIs
steps.description: Understand how large language models generate text through next-token prediction. Master prompt engineering techniques: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and structured output prompting. Integrate OpenAI and Anthropic APIs in Python, manage API keys securely, and control generation with temperature and top-p sampling.

steps.title: ReAct Agents and Tool Calling
steps.description: Implement the ReAct (Reason + Act) loop from scratch: the agent reasons about a goal, selects an action, calls a tool, observes the result, and iterates. Define tools as Python functions exposed via function-calling schemas (OpenAI tools format). Build agents that can search the web, run code, and query databases.

steps.title: LangChain and LangGraph for Agent Workflows
steps.description: Use LangChain's LCEL (LangChain Expression Language) to compose chains of prompts, retrievers, and parsers. Model stateful, branching agent workflows as directed graphs with LangGraph. Implement conditional edges and human-in-the-loop approval steps. Persist agent state across turns with checkpointers.

steps.title: Memory, Context Management, and Multi-Agent Systems
steps.description: Distinguish short-term (in-context), episodic (vector store), and semantic (knowledge graph) memory. Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground agents in private documents. Design multi-agent systems where specialised sub-agents are orchestrated by a supervisor agent using message passing.

steps.title: Observability, Guardrails, and Production Readiness
steps.description: Instrument agents with LangSmith tracing for visibility into each reasoning step and tool call. Implement input/output guardrails to detect prompt injection, hallucination, and out-of-scope requests. Apply retry logic and fallback chains for reliability. Package agents as a FastAPI service with health checks and rate limiting.

title: Automation with n8n
description: A practical introduction to workflow automation with n8n, the open-source low-code platform. Learners progress from installing n8n locally through connecting APIs, transforming data with JavaScript expressions, building AI-augmented workflows, and deploying reliable automations to production. No prior programming experience is required, though JavaScript basics are beneficial.
competencies: HTTP Request and REST API integration
JavaScript expressions and the Code node
conditional logic with IF and Switch nodes

steps.title: n8n Setup and Core Concepts
steps.description: Install n8n via npm or Docker and explore the canvas UI. Understand the execution model: triggers fire workflows; nodes process data; each node receives items (JSON objects) and passes transformed items downstream. Build a first workflow: a Schedule trigger that fetches a public API and logs results to a Google Sheet.
competencies_developed: HTTP Request and REST API integration

steps.title: Data Transformation and Expressions
steps.description: Use n8n's expression editor ({{ }}) and built-in methods to reshape data: access nested JSON fields, format dates with Luxon, manipulate strings, and compute derived values. Apply the Set node to normalise payloads and the Code node (JavaScript) for complex transformations that go beyond expressions.
competencies_developed: JavaScript expressions and the Code node

steps.title: Conditional Logic, Loops, and Error Handling
steps.description: Route items through different branches using IF and Switch nodes. Process arrays of items with SplitInBatches and Merge nodes. Configure Error Trigger workflows and per-node retry policies. Build a notification workflow that sends a Slack alert when a downstream node fails.
competencies_developed: conditional logic with IF and Switch nodes

steps.title: Webhooks, APIs, and Authentication
steps.description: Create inbound Webhook nodes that accept POST payloads from external services (e.g. GitHub, Stripe). Secure webhooks with header authentication and IP allow-lists. Use the HTTP Request node with OAuth2, API key, and Basic Auth credential types. Build a two-way sync between a CRM and a project management tool.
competencies_developed: HTTP Request and REST API integration
conditional logic with IF and Switch nodes

steps.title: AI-Augmented Workflows and Production Deployment
steps.description: Incorporate n8n's native LangChain nodes to add an LLM step into existing workflows: summarise emails, classify support tickets, or generate draft replies. Connect to vector stores for RAG-powered lookups. Deploy n8n on a VPS with environment-variable secrets management, configure execution log retention, and set up monitoring alerts.
